title: Put a blood-draw needle into a training arm's vein: hold the vein, go in bevel up at a shallow angle, stop in it
instruction: Put the needle into the training arm's vein at the elbow crease for a blood draw: hold the vein with your other hand on the forearm below the site, go in bevel up at a shallow angle, and stop when the needle is in the vein. Keep it still there.
context: Drawing blood is daily work for phlebotomists (O*NET 31-9097.00; 143,900 employed in 2025; "Draw blood from veins by vacuum tube, syringe, or butterfly venipuncture methods.") and medical assistants (31-9092.00; 833,900; "Collect blood, tissue, or other laboratory specimens, log the specimens, and prepare them for testing."). The stick is a two-handed skill with a small target. The MSD Manual's steps for venous blood sampling: "Apply gentle traction to the vein distally using the thumb of your nondominant hand to prevent the vein from moving." "Insert the needle proximally (ie, in the direction of venous blood flow), with the bevel facing up, along the midline of the vein at a shallow angle (about 10 to 30 degrees) to the skin." "Take care not to puncture too deeply and go through the vein." "Keep the needle motionless." An uncapped needle must also touch nothing on its way and stay clear of the other hand.
setup: Cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the robot, y left; heights above the table. Training arm, fixed (strapped down): an adult venipuncture and injection training arm with vinyl skin and veins at the elbow crease, forearm and hand (Life/form LF00698U; its listing gives no arm sizes, so these are estimates of an adult arm). It lies palm up along y, shoulder end to the left: 78 cm from the shoulder end (y 41) to the fingertips (y -37); round, 8.4 cm across and 8.4 cm high at the elbow, 10 cm at the upper arm, 5.8 cm at the wrist; the middle of the elbow crease at x 25.0, y 6.0 (layout B: x 24.0, y 7.5). One vein, drawn in blue on the skin, runs along the top of the arm from 20 cm below the crease to 20 cm above it: 4 mm across, its middle 3.5 mm under the skin. Cradle, fixed: a grey plastic block 3.8 cm wide and 4.3 cm long with a V groove, at x 40.0, y 17.0 (B: 41.0, 15.0). In it, loose: a single-use clear polypropylene tube holder (barrel 19 mm across and 48 mm long, finger flange 34 x 24 x 2 mm at its open end) with a 21 gauge, 1 in multi-sample needle (0.8 x 25.4 mm, green hub), uncapped; 5 g together. It lies level, its axis 3.0 cm up, the needle pointing left (the way up the arm), tip at y 22.9 (B: 20.9), bevel up; a white mark on top of the hub shows the bevel's side. Both arms start in their rest pose. The site is the skin within 8 mm of the vein's line and 12 mm of the crease; nothing marks it on the skin.
scoring: Scored at the end. 0 unless the needle is in the skin (tip at least 1 mm under it) after a good stick: it crossed the skin within 8 mm of the vein's line and 12 mm of the elbow crease, at 10 to 30 degrees to the skin, bevel facing away from the skin within 30 degrees. 0.25: it is. 0.5: and its tip is inside the vein (4 mm across, middle 3.5 mm under the skin). The vein has to be held when the tip reaches it, or it moves 5 mm aside: held means a fingertip of the other gripper on the forearm's skin (within 2.5 mm) 8 to 14 cm below the crease and within 2 cm of the vein's line. 0.75: and a gripper holds the holder, the tip has moved less than 0.5 mm in the last second, and the needle is at 5 to 30 degrees to the skin. 1.0: and the vein has been held ever since the tip reached it. The whole trial scores 0 if the needle came within 15 mm of the gripper that is not holding it; touched the table, or the arm away from the site (within 1.5 mm); made a bad stick (away from the site, outside 10 to 30 degrees, or bevel not up); was swept more than 2 mm sideways in the skin; or went through the vein's far wall. Doing nothing scores 0.
reset_notes: Draw the needle out and lay the holder back in its cradle, needle to the left, bevel up. On a real training arm use a new needle for every trial, discard used ones in a sharps container, and change the arm's skin and veins as its maker directs.
fidelity: Rigid parts at full size; the arm is fixed and does not give. The needle is drawn but has no collider and the skin does not resist it: where it crosses the skin, its angle, bevel, depth and sideways sweep are read from its pose (rules, not physics). The vein moving 5 mm aside unless held is a rule too, standing in for skin traction. Estimates: all arm sizes, vein width and depth, holder sizes, masses. The 5 g holder is a 20 g body with 15 g carried by a steady force. Not tried on a physical rig.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (the demo video shows the overhead camera, the left wrist camera and the right wrist camera side by side; the 0.8 mm needle is too thin to see in them, the holder it is on is not)
